statement: gocryptfs encrypts filenames with EME, preserves directory structure, and uses per-directory IVs against cross-directory name correlation; a Directory IV Poisoning attack exists in the Dragon model.
evidence_in_source: primary citation (web-verified by research agent on 2026-08-29)

location: §9 gocryptfs comparison L396; leak table L422
statement: CryFS hides sizes with fixed chunks and flattens directories at heavy cost: 41s vs 10.9s extract and 42s vs 5.1s checksum (Linux), 1,124s vs 456s (Windows vs cppcryptfs); securefs flattens with AES-SIV names; EncFS hides nothing by default.
evidence_in_source: third-party measurement cited (gocryptfs comparison page), not an Entrybound experiment
research_needed: Measure size-hiding costs in the archive setting; filesystem figures do not transfer directly.

statement: borg encrypts chunk contents, metadata structures, archive names and timestamps; its plaintext repo header carries magic, format version and chunk ID; chunk sizes and file discovery order/proximity unavoidably leak.
evidence_in_source: primary citation (web-verified by research agent on 2026-08-29)

statement: borg 2 authenticates object type (ro_type) so an attacker cannot change an object's type or relocate content between object IDs (borg 1.x needed a separate TAM); object type and identity should be bound into authenticated data.

statement: RFC 8725 (BCP 225, Feb 2020) documents JWT 'alg':'none' acceptance and RS256-to-HS256 substitution using the RSA public key as HMAC secret, rooted in libraries not enforcing that the header algorithm matches the operation.

statement: TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446) decomposed cipher suites into AEAD plus HKDF hash, negotiating key exchange and signatures separately, collapsing TLS 1.2's combinatorial explosion.

statement: TLS 1.3 aggressively pruned all non-AEAD symmetric algorithms, static RSA and static DH, compression, DSA, and custom DHE groups.

statement: TLS 1.3 downgrade sentinel: a server negotiating TLS 1.2 sets the last eight bytes of ServerHello.random to a fixed value so clients detect forced downgrade.
evidence_in_source: primary citation (web-verified by research agent on 2026-08-29)

statement: PGP's 25 years of accreted algorithm agility ended in the LibrePGP fork, two incompatible specifications disputing algorithm additions and removals: a governance failure, not a security upgrade.
